title: screening_fidelity_result.json -- screening report vs ground truth v0.1
description: Produced by screening-fidelity, the one local stage harness-guardrails-dev D1 admits to ground truth. Records how closely a screening report agrees with the adjuster's real report, per templates/rubric-screening-fidelity.md. Distinct from screening_rubric_result (reference-free writing quality) and from evaluation_result (the deferred Unit 11 suite over draft reports); the three answer different questions and their scores are never combined. LEAK BOUNDARY: this contract has no field anywhere for verbatim ground-truth text. The ground-truth side carries a locator and, where the comparison needs one, a short field value (<=200 chars: a date, a code, an amount, a diagnosis name). Narrative passages from the answer key must not be copied into rationale or description either -- a result file naming what the answer key says, sentence by sentence, is the answer key. Screening-side quotes are required instead, because the report is not privileged material and a score with no quotation cannot be checked.

rubric_version.description: Which revision of templates/rubric-screening-fidelity.md produced this score. Scores from different rubric revisions are not comparable.

target_report_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the scored screening report's bytes, binding the score to one exact document version.

scoring_run_id.description: The run that PRODUCED this score, which is not the run that produced the report. Inherited `run_id` names the latter -- it is the scored artifact's own run and must stay that way, or the score stops being traceable to the exact pipeline execution it describes. A separate field is therefore the only place a scoring run can be recorded. Deliberately not bound to the RUN_YYYYMMDD_N pattern: a scoring pass is identified by what it scored and under which rubric (e.g. fidelity_bundle_20260827_8002), and forcing it into the pipeline's run vocabulary would make the two indistinguishable at a glance.

dimensions.description: F1-F4, each exactly once. A dimension that cannot apply is applicable:false with a reason -- omitting it would drop it from the weighted denominator with nothing on the record to say so.

fidelity_score.description: Weighted over applicable headline dimensions only (F1 50, F2 30, F3 20). F4 is excluded by design: conclusion direction is discretionary, and a report that correctly declines to assert one would otherwise be penalised for good practice.

core_field_mismatch.description: True when any core field (주진단명, 사고일, 청구 담보, 부지급/감액 사유) compared as 'mismatch'. Forces verdict 'divergent' whatever the score says -- a report with the wrong diagnosis is not 80% aligned. A core field merely missing from the screening report does NOT set this: writing something wrong and failing to write it are different failures.

verdict.description: divergent when core_field_mismatch; else aligned at >=80, partial at >=60, divergent below.

findings.description: What to change, numbered stably so a human disposition can reference one. An empty array means no change was called for, not that findings were skipped.

routing_config_version.description: config_version of the routing config the denominators came from (claim_analysis_routing.v0.1). Scores taken against different field universes are not comparable, and this records which one was used.

out_of_universe_items.description: Empty is a valid outcome, and means the answer key stayed inside the configured universe.

allOf.$comment: Each dimension id appears exactly once. uniqueItems cannot express this on objects differing in other fields.
A core-field mismatch pins the verdict. Stated in the schema so a result cannot be written that reports one and calls itself aligned.

ground_truth_access.description: How the answer key was reached. Recorded so a reader can confirm the D1 conditions held at scoring time without taking the agent's word for it.

version.description: Which artifact class this read was for. 'screening' -- the screening report -- is the only value this stage may use; v1/v2 name a draft-report review and the DAO refuses them here. They stay expressible so results written under the earlier gate still validate.

caller_stage.description: The stage name passed to dao.py read-ground-truth. Const because this contract exists for exactly one stage.

screening_stage_passed.description: The report's own run finished: screening_report is 'passed' in run state. This is the precondition the DAO enforces on this path -- not a human sign-off. Fidelity scoring measures pipeline performance, so it does not gate on a reader (owner's decision, 2026-08-26); what it does refuse is scoring a report whose run failed, which would be a number about nothing. Recording it here makes the condition visible in the artifact instead of implied.

source.description: Which tree served the answer key. 'data_ground_truth' is the intaked case, whose GT passed a D2 per-file review. 'handoff_bundle' is a case whose GT was quarantined by a corpus split and never intaked, read in place from _handoff/ -- the gates are identical, but the provenance is not, and a score should not hide which one it rests on. Absent means 'data_ground_truth': results written before the bundle path existed stay valid.

source_bundle.description: Bundle name under _handoff/ when source is 'handoff_bundle'. Names the exact assembly the answer key came from, since a bundle is hand-assembled and can be rebuilt differently.

ground_truth_ref.description: Where in the answer key the comparison looked. A locator, never a passage.

locator.description: Page, section, or field label -- e.g. 'p.3 사정 결과' or '진단명란'. Not a sentence from the document.

dimension_id.description: F1 factual field agreement / F2 issue-prediction recall / F3 required-document agreement / F4 conclusion direction.

weight.description: F1 50, F2 30, F3 20, F4 0 (excluded from the headline).

score.description: This dimension's own 0-100. Null for F4, which is not scored, and for an inapplicable dimension.

rationale.description: How the number was reached. Describe the comparison; do not quote the answer key to explain it.

screening_quotes.description: Verbatim lines from the screening report. At least one when the dimension applies.

discretionary_agreement_rate.description: Reported beside the headline, never folded into it. Under P3 a screening report may correctly decline to assert a discretionary value and score 0 here for being right.

document_comparisons.description: F3 rows. document_kind uses the routing config's own vocabulary, and the denominator is required_documents_by_case_type for the case's determined types.

conclusion_agreement.description: F4 only. 'screening_declined' is not a failure: declining to assert a discretionary conclusion on thin material is what P3 asks for.

allOf.$comment: A scored, applicable headline dimension must carry a number.
F4 is excluded from the headline: it carries no score and must state its agreement instead.

field_name.description: Human label for the row, normally the config's label_ko. Convenience only -- field_id is the identity.

field_kind.description: 'fact' when the answer is stated somewhere in the material, 'discretionary' when a professional arrives at it (과실률, 손해액, 소득 기준). Classify by where the answer comes from, not by how hard it was.

core_field.description: Mirrors the config's critical_conflict_field -- 'fields whose disagreement can change a determination' (run_consistency_check.critical_field_ids), 32 of the 64. Read from the config, never chosen here. A mismatch on one pins the verdict to divergent.

ground_truth_value.description: A short field value only -- a date, a code, an amount, a name. Never a sentence, never a passage; the cap is the enforcement.

match_kind.description: 'not_applicable' is for a field the pipeline deliberately does not extract (extraction_wave or activation_basis 'deferred'). The answer key may carry such a value; not carrying it is not a miss, so the row leaves the denominator -- as does missing_in_ground_truth, where the report carried more than the key.

screening_absence_kind.description: How the REPORT presented the absence -- 'declared' when it scoped it ('확인 불가'), 'silent' when it said nothing at all. Kept alongside pipeline_unavailable_reason because the two answer different questions: why the value is missing, and whether the reader was told.

field_id.description: The routing config's own field_id (config/claim_analysis/claim_analysis_routing_v0.1.json, fields[].field_id). That list is the denominator, not a set the scorer assembles: the first two cases were scored over hand-picked sets of 11 and 13 fact fields, which made their scores incomparable and left nothing to appeal to.

field_grade.description: From whichever axis the field declares: medical_advisory_grade for a medical domain, priority_grade for a legal_factual one. The config enforces exactly one of the two (never both, never neither), so this needs no default. Do not merge the axes -- ranking 과실비율 on what a physician needs is what once put the sole basis of a liability determination at grade C.

legal_authority.description: For a legal_factual field: whether the value is a fact a document states or an opinion a party's counsel reached. Two opposing 법률의견서 are not a records contradiction, so a report that preserved both instead of choosing is following the rule, not omitting a value.

pipeline_resolution_status.description: What claim_analysis_result recorded for this field_id. Copied, never inferred.

pipeline_unavailable_reason.description: Upstream's own account of why a value is absent. Supersedes the rubric's declared/silent guess: a value missing because the document kind is absent, one the document had but left blank, and one never mentioned anywhere are three different failures that the two-value split scored identically.

gt_issue_label.description: A topic label for the answer key's issue, in the scorer's words -- '배상책임 성립 여부'. Not the answer key's sentence.

predicted.description: Whether the screening report raised this issue. Different wording still counts: what matters is whether the same question was put on the table.

screening_only_issue.description: An issue the report raised that the answer key does not address. Recorded, never scored -- the PoC question is agreement with the adjuster, not improvement on them.

classification.description: 손사_미기재: a real question the adjuster's document does not take up. 중복: the same issue already counted under another id. 오탐: not a real issue.

verdict.description: 'over' (flagged as missing but the answer key never needed it) is recorded and NOT counted against the score: an over-broad document request costs effort, while a document the adjuster relied on and the report never named means the next stage proceeds without it.

out_of_universe_item.description: Something the answer key relied on that has no field_id and no document_kind in the routing config. Recorded, never scored. Binding the denominators to the pipeline otherwise leaves the rubric able to measure only what the pipeline already knows to look for; 사고경위서 is the live example -- the answer key's evidence for the accident narrative in both scored cases, and absent from document_kinds entirely.
